frontier.hypothesis: The real 24-byte local at sp+0x50..0x67 is a referenced aggregate that the source declares after the 8-byte icon record, and recovering it is now a hard prerequisite for any submission - the current s16 sp50[12] inflation of IconC70 is KNOWN WRONG, contradicted by func_80069898's four-field contract and func_8006B120's frame.
frontier.mechanism: Correctness of the submitted C, not codegen. GCC 2.7.2 drops an unreferenced local outright (s12 measured frame 128 -> 104), so whatever occupies those 24 bytes is read, written or address-taken somewhere in the function - which means the target's own instruction stream must touch it, or it is passed by address to one of the six callees (func_8007352C, func_8006E480, SetDrawMode, AddPrim, func_80070F78, func_8006ECF4, func_80072E10, func_80073200).
frontier.next_probe: Disassemble asm/funcs/func_80070C70.s and enumerate EVERY $sp-relative access with an offset in 0x50..0x67 (there appear to be none in the objdump extract tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s12/tgt.txt, so check the raw .s for addiu $aN,$sp,0x50-style address materialisations feeding a call). Then do the same for func_800720FC, whose spare region is 32 bytes at 0x50..0x6F - two functions with the same idiom and different sizes should identify the type. Cross-check func_8006F97C (active queue sibling, same TU, same func_80069898 call) and propagate the corrected 8-byte IconC70 to its ledger either way.

frontier.hypothesis: The whole remaining 22 is still one cluster - the missing cse_set_around_loop hoist of the D_800A3558 and D_800A35B0 reads out of the second loop body - and the do/while chassis cannot reach it by any C spelling, so the only two live routes are (a) making the top-test chassis' three orphan spill pseudos not exist, or (b) finding a do/while spelling in which the guard's loads survive into the body through ordinary cse rather than cse_set_around_loop.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c:7933 gates the transform on REG_LOOP_TEST_P, set only by jump.c:2253 in duplicate_loop_exit_test, which requires a top-test loop; the top-test loop in turn pays three combine-orphaned (use (reg)) pseudos typed ST_REGS (H-s10-1) worth 24 frame bytes. s12 priced that trade at 9 points against us with both chassis fully levered, and re-killed all three known orphan-removal levers on the improved chassis.
frontier.next_probe: Route (a) is the only untried angle left and it is a combine question, not an RA one: read tools/gcc-2.7.2/combine.c:2089 and 10730-10850 with tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s10/w/sec.combine open, and work out what property of the target's insn stream let its REG_DEAD notes find homes (the target has the guard copy AND vars=80, so its build did NOT take the newi2pat path that orphans p116/p168/p173). Regenerate the dumps for the 31-point a3 body first via pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80070C70 - every existing dump is of the 49-point body.

frontier.hypothesis: The prologue tie (addiu $a0,$sp,24 against addu $s0,$zero,$zero) and the guard block's instruction order are reachable from the two remaining unswept statement-order axes: the four statements of the FIRST loop body, and the order of the three pre-guard statements (the AddPrim tail, prim.p_geom = ctx[8], and the guard test itself).
frontier.mechanism: Both are sched1/reorg outcomes downstream of what else is ready in the same cycle. s11 swept six positions of var_s0 = 0; inside the guarded region and s12 swept the position outside it (54) plus a pointer local for &prim (38) and the ctx read hoist (60); the first loop's own four-statement order has still only had two of six orders measured, and it moved once already (between s11's q3 and r1).
frontier.next_probe: Install memory/grind/func_80070C70/candidate.c, regenerate the objdump diff with tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s12/dis.sh, then enumerate the remaining four orders of the first loop's body statements (prim.mode, prim.link read, prim.code store, the func_8007352C call) and the three orders of the pre-guard statements, scoring with tmp/grind/func_80070C70/s12/score.sh.
